PRESIDENT'S ORDER 9 OF 1979
PAKISTAN (AUDIT AND
ACCOUNTS) (AMENDMENT) ORDER, 1979
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part I, 15th May 1979]
No. F. 17(2)/79-Pub.-The following Order made by the
President is hereby published for general information :-
In pursuance of the Proclamation of the fifth day of
July 1977, read with the Laws (Continuance in Force) Order, 1977 (C. M. L. A.
Order No. 1 of 1977), and in exercise of all powers enabling him in that
behalf, the President is pleased to make the following Order:-
1. Short title and
commencement.-(1) This
Order may be called the Pakistan (Audit and Accounts) (Amendment) Order, 1979.
(2) It shall come into force at once and shall be
deemed to have taken effect on the fifth day of December 1978.
2. Amendment of Article 6,
P. O. No. 21 of 1973.--In
the Pakistan (Audit and Accounts] Order, 1973 (President's Order No. 21 of
1973), hereinafter referred to as the said Order, in Article 6, for clause
(1-A) the following shall be substituted, namely :-
"(1-A) A person to whom leave is granted under
clause (1), shall, if the leave granted expires after the termination of his
tenure of office, be deemed, for the purpose only of the appointment of a
successor, to have ceased to hold once on the day on which the leave
commences."
3. Insertion of a new
Article 6-A, P. O. No. 21 of 1973.-In the said Order, after Article 6 amended as aforesaid, the following
new Article shall be inserted, namely: --
"6-A. Retirement from
service.-A person who,
immediately before his, appointment as Auditor-General, was in the service of
Pakistan shall stand retired from service on the termination of his tenure of
office or, if the leave granted to him expires after the termination of his
tenure of office, on the expiry of the leave."
BYE-LAWS FOR THE
REGISTRATION AND CONTROL OF DOGS AND THE PREVENTION OF RABIES WITHIN THE TAXILA
CANTONMENT
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part II, 3rd May, 1979]
S. R. O. 378(1)/79.-The following bye laws for the
registration and control of dogs and the prevention of rabies within the Taxila
Cantonment, made by the Cantonment Board, Taxila, in exercise of the powers
conferred by section 119 of the Cantonment Act, 1924 (I1 of 1924), read with
section 283 thereof, are published for general information, the same having
been previously published by the said Board, and approved and confirmed by the
Federal Government, as required by subsection (1) of section 284 of the said
Act, namely :-
1. In these bye-laws, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context, "Veterinary Officer" means any
Veterinary Officer in the Army or the Cantonment Board, or a Veterinary
Assistant in Government service on duty in the Cantonment.
2. Every person owning or keeping a dog or otherwise
in charge thereof within the Cantonment limits shall, within fifteen days from
the publication of these bye-laws or within fifteen days after bringing a dog
within such limits, as the case may be, cause such dog to be registered in a
register kept for the purpose,--
(a) in the case of dogs kept in the lines of a
military Unit, by the Officer Commanding the Unit ; and
(b) in the case of all other dogs, at the office of
the Board :--
Provided that no registration shall be necessary-
(i) if the owner of the dog is the Federal Government
or a Provincial Government ; or
(ii) if the dog is kept within the Cantonment limits
temporarily for a period not exceeding one month ; and
(iii) in the case of puppies of not more than three
months of age.
3. An application for registration shall be in the
form appended to these bye-laws.
4. The registration shall be valid up to the 30th
June next following and the owner or keeper of a dog already registered shall,
on or before the Ist July, make an application to the proper authority for its
renewal.
5.-(1) A list of all dogs registered by an officer
Commanding the Unit each year shall be forwarded by him to the Executive
Officer by the 15th
